structure: Part 2, the start of the journey, read at commit c2078fb (the checkout's HEAD). Read in full: the three DR2.1 views notification-type.html (57 lines), origin-of-the-import.html (179) and what-are-you-importing.html (150); partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html (31); the list files countries.js (79), country-region-prefixes.js (44), commodities.js (14, now a loader over generated/commodities-live.json plus commodity-curated.js), commodities-germinal-products.js (21, a loader over generated/commodities-germinal.json), commodities-testing3.js (95, four extra live commodities the DR2.1 search adds), commodity-curated.js (77), generated/README.md (131), generated/commodities-germinal.json (723, all 18 entries) and utils/commodity-search-data.js (39); and app/routes.js lines 97-307, 510-547, 608-945, 1139-1165, 12130-12220 and 12717-12926. To pin down behaviour the handlers call, it also read small helpers outside those ranges: hasJourneyUpdates and ensurePrototypeNotificationReference (320-385), resetNotificationJourneySession (427-487), getJourneyBackLink (596-606), isGerminalProductCommodity (954-956), the journey save and continue redirects (1782-1824), getIdentificationSpeciesLabel (2224-2237), hasGerminalProductsOnly (5167-5178), getDashboardListPath (7879-7889), generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference (9073-9102), allowsBlankJourneyAnswers and applyJourneyValidation (10352-10382), and the shared partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html. Covered: GET /create-notification (what it resets, the category shortcut, where it sends the user); the notification type page (route, caption, heading, five options, error, back link, where each type and the template journey lead); the origin page (country search and its 41 options, region of origin question, prefix by country and suffix input, internal reference, validation, saving and branches); the commodity page (inset text, search label and hints by type, selection panel, help details, buttons, validation, filtering by type, saving, removal, display titles); how the country, prefix, germinal, extra live and curated lists are built; and the generated live catalogue as generated/README.md describes it. The 8,259-line commodities-live.json and the client-side search scripts were not read, as the partition directs, so the previous extract's per-commodity live-animal claims, which read a hand-written commodities.js that no longer exists, are not carried forward.

claims.statement: GET /create-notification clears the current notification journey from the session but keeps the address book additions, draft notifications, deleted notification references, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted template ids and the per-version session nests.
GET /create-notification also clears any in-progress template creation flag.
In Design Release 2.1, GET /create-notification with no category in the query string sends the user to the notification type page (/notification-type).

GET /create-notification with a recognised category query (for example from a category dashboard) skips the notification type page: it records that the journey started from a category dashboard, starts the notification with that type, and sends the user straight to /origin-of-the-import.

The code says the notification type question is skipped when the user starts from the live animals or germinal products dashboard, because the type is already known, and is asked only when there is no category, such as from the overall dashboard.

Starting a notification sets its type, sets its status to Draft, clears the template-creation flag, gives it a new notification reference (in the design releases) and saves it as a draft notification.
claims.quote:
sessionData.notificationType = notificationType
  sessionData.notificationStatus = 'Draft'
  delete sessionData.isCreatingTemplate

  if (isDesignRelease2SessionData(sessionData)) {
    sessionData.notificationReference = generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference(sessionData)
  }

  persistDraftNotification(sessionData)

claims.statement: A new design-release notification reference has the form GBN-AG-26- followed by six random upper-case letters or digits, and is chosen so it does not clash with the fixed sample reference, the current reference, dashboard notifications, drafts or submitted notifications.
claims.note: mechanism: the random code is padded with 0 to six characters, and up to 25 attempts are made.

claims.statement: Outside Design Release 2.1, GET and POST /notification-type redirect to /create-notification: the notification type page exists only in DR2.1.
GET /notification-type clears any previous errors before showing the page.
The notification type page's heading, shown as the radio group's legend, is "What are you importing?".
claims.quote: html: 'About the consignment What are you importing?', isPageHeading: true,

claims.statement: The notification type page shows the caption "About the consignment" above its heading.
The notification type page's page name is "What are you importing?", the same as the commodity page that follows origin.
The notification type page offers five radio options, in this order: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products.
claims.quote:
{ value: 'live-animals', text: 'Live animals' },
  { value: 'germinal-products', text: 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)' },
  { value: 'plants-for-planting', text: 'Plants for planting' },
  { value: 'potatoes', text: 'Potatoes (seed and ware)' },
  { value: 'wood-products', text: 'Wood products' }

claims.statement: None of the notification type options has hint text, and the radio group has no hint: the options carry only a value and text, and the radios set no hint.
The notification type page pre-selects the type already held for the notification.

When no type is stored, the notification's type is worked out from its selections: germinal products only means germinal products, and selected species that are all live-animal species means live animals; otherwise the type is empty.
If no notification type is selected, the page shows the error "Select what you are importing", both inline and in the error summary, linking to the notificationType field.
The notification type, origin and commodity pages show their errors in an error summary titled "There is a problem".

The server accepts a notification type given either as its value or as its display label (case-insensitive), and also recognises three types the page does not offer: products of animal origin or animal by-products, high-risk food or feed of non-animal origin, and plants, plant products or other objects.
claims.note: mechanism: normalises the notificationType value from a form post or a category query string. 'potatoes' is accepted as a label as well as 'potatoes (seed and ware)'.

claims.statement: The notification type page has a single "Continue" button and no save-and-return-to-overview button or cancel link.
claims.note: In the shared journey-form-actions partial, a notification in Amend status or a template being edited from review shows a different set of buttons regardless of these options.

claims.statement: The notification type page's back link goes to the dashboard (/), or to /templates when the user is creating a template; the service navigation highlights Dashboard, or Templates when creating a template.
Choosing a notification type marks the journey as not started from a category dashboard.
Changing the notification type to a different one from before clears every selected commodity and species.
When creating a template, choosing a notification type stores the type, sets the status to Draft and sends the user to /templates/create instead of the origin page.

Choosing a notification type starts a new notification (reference, Draft status, saved draft) when there is no notification reference yet; when there is one, it updates the type and saves the draft again.
After a valid notification type is chosen, every type (including plants for planting, potatoes and wood products) goes on to /origin-of-the-import.
The three start pages show an Alpha phase banner reading "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.", with the feedback link pointing at #.
GET and POST /origin-of-the-import make sure the notification has a design-release reference (GBN-AG-26-...), generating one if it has none or has a reference in another format.

The origin page's back link goes to /templates/create when creating a template, to the category dashboard list for the notification's type when the journey started from a category dashboard, and otherwise to /notification-type.
claims.note: getDashboardListPath falls back to /live-animals in DR2.1 when the type has no dashboard category.

claims.statement: The origin page and the commodity page show the notification status block (which carries the notification reference) above the form; the reference falls back to the fixed sample reference when none is held.
claims.note: The status partial itself belongs to part 1; that it shows the reference is read from the render data passing notificationReference.

claims.statement: The origin page has the caption "About the consignment" and the heading "Origin of the import", which is also its page name.
claims.quote:
About the consignment

Origin of the import

claims.statement: The origin page asks for the country of origin under the sub-heading "Country of origin".

The country of origin is chosen through a search box with the placeholder "Search for a country", a search button ("Search", visually hidden text) and a results list labelled "Country search results"; the chosen country is submitted in a hidden countryOfOrigin field.
The country search has a polite live region for announcing search status to screen readers.
The country search shows no hint text: the country form group holds a heading, an error slot and the search, with no hint element.
The country of origin field shows an inline error (prefixed "Error:" for screen readers) when the server sets a countryOfOrigin error.
The country search box and the hidden country field are filled with the country already saved when the origin page is shown again.

The countries offered for country of origin are the 27 EU member states: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Ireland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Sweden.

The country list also offers 11 territories, each shown as "Name (Parent)": Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), Ceuta (Spain), French Guiana (France), Guadeloupe (France), Madeira (Portugal), Martinique (France), Mayotte (France), Melilla (Spain), Reunion (France) and Saint Martin (France).
The country list also offers the 3 crown dependencies, shown as Guernsey (United Kingdom), Jersey (United Kingdom) and Isle of Man (United Kingdom).
The 41 country options are sorted alphabetically by their displayed label, and the stored value is the displayed label (so a territory is stored as "Name (Parent)").
The country of origin list holds no country outside the EU, its territories and the crown dependencies, so no third country can be chosen as the origin: the page is sent only this list.
The origin page asks "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" with Yes and No radios.
claims.quote: Does the consignment have a region of origin code?

claims.statement: The region of origin question has the hint "Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now."
claims.quote: Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.

claims.statement: The region of origin radios show an inline error when the server sets a regionOfOriginRequired error.
Answering Yes to the region of origin question reveals a region of origin code field beneath the Yes option; No reveals nothing.
The region of origin code field is labelled "Enter the region of origin code" with the hint "Enter up to 5 characters."
claims.quote:
Enter the region of origin code
  </label>
  <div id="region-of-origin-code-hint" class="govuk-hint app-region-origin-code__hint">
    Enter up to 5 characters.

claims.statement: The region of origin code input accepts at most 5 characters, with autocomplete and spellcheck turned off.
The region of origin code input shows the chosen country's two-letter prefix in front of it (hidden from screen readers), so the user types only the suffix.
The region of origin code input shows an inline error (prefixed "Error:" for screen readers) when the server sets a regionOfOriginCodeSuffix error.
The region prefix map is also sent to the page alongside the country list, so the prefix can follow the country the user picks.
claims.note: The client script that swaps the prefix is out of scope; that the prefix follows the pick is inferred from the map being sent.

claims.statement: Region of origin prefixes are the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the chosen country, one per member state: Austria AT, Belgium BE, Bulgaria BG, Croatia HR, Cyprus CY, Czech Republic CZ, Denmark DK, Estonia EE, Finland FI, France FR, Germany DE, Greece GR, Hungary HU, Italy IT, Latvia LV, Lithuania LT, Luxembourg LU, Malta MT, Netherlands NL, Poland PL, Portugal PT, Republic of Ireland IE, Romania RO, Slovakia SK, Slovenia SI, Spain ES, Sweden SE.
claims.quote: // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 prefixes shown before the region of origin code suffix

claims.statement: Territories take their parent state's prefix (Azores and Madeira PT, Canary Islands ES, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Reunion and Saint Martin FR), except Ceuta, which is XC, and Melilla, which is XL.
The crown dependencies have their own prefixes: Guernsey GG, Isle of Man IM, Jersey JE.
With no country chosen, or a country missing from the prefix map, no prefix is shown.
The region of origin code suffix is trimmed and converted to upper case when saved.
With Yes, a country and a suffix, the full region of origin code is saved as prefix, hyphen, suffix (for example FR-ABC12); if the country has no prefix, the code is the suffix alone.
Answering No (or not answering) to the region of origin question clears any saved region of origin code and suffix.
claims.quote:
req.session.data.regionOfOriginCodeSuffix = regionOfOriginRequired === 'Yes'
      ? (regionOfOriginCodeSuffix || null)
      : null
    req.session.data.regionOfOriginCode = null

claims.statement: Answering Yes with a suffix but no country keeps the suffix but saves no full region of origin code, because the full code is built only when a country is held.
When the page is shown again, the suffix field is filled from the saved suffix, or else from the saved full code with everything up to the first hyphen removed.
A saved full region of origin code with no hyphen is shown in the suffix field whole.
claims.note: mechanism: reads the saved regionOfOriginCode back into the suffix input.

claims.statement: If Yes is chosen and no region of origin code is entered, the page shows the error "Enter the region of origin code", inline and in the summary, linking to the code input.

When the user is creating a template in DR2.1, the origin and commodity pages show no validation errors at all: the errors are passed through a filter that keeps only errors for answers that were entered, and these pages pass no entered answers, so a blank region code or an empty commodity selection can be saved.
claims.note: Neither call passes submittedValues, so every error key is dropped in a template; outside a template the validation is returned unchanged.

claims.statement: The origin page does not validate the country of origin: a user can continue with no country chosen, and no error message for a missing or invalid country is defined, although the view has a slot to show one.
The origin page does not require an answer to "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?": no error message for a missing answer is defined, although the view has a slot to show one.
The source gives no format rule for the region of origin code suffix beyond the 5-character limit on the input: no allowed characters, minimum length or server-side length check.

The origin page has an optional text field labelled "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)" with the hint "Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank."
claims.quote: text: "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)",
claims.note: Hint quote: "Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank."

claims.statement: The internal reference is trimmed and saved, or cleared when left blank; it has no validation.
The country of origin and region of origin answer are saved as soon as the origin form is posted, before validation, so they are kept even when the page shows an error.
claims.quote:
req.session.data.countryOfOrigin = countryOfOrigin || null
  req.session.data.regionOfOriginRequired = regionOfOriginRequired || null

claims.statement: The origin page normally shows a single "Save and continue" button, with no save-and-return-to-overview button and no cancel link: it turns both off and the shared actions default the button text.
Saving the origin page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or the review page.

A valid origin page continues to /what-are-you-importing, or back to the notification hub when opened from the hub, to the review page when opened from review, or to the template review when editing a template.
When the origin or commodity page is opened from the notification hub, the form carries from=hub so that saving returns to the hub.
Origin details count as complete only when a country is chosen and the region question is answered, and, when the answer is Yes, a region of origin code suffix is held.
The commodity page can be opened without origin details: its guard against missing origin never redirects.
GET /what-are-you-importing makes sure the notification has a design-release reference and clears any leftover search text before showing the page.
The commodity page has the caption "About the consignment" and the heading "What are you importing?", which is also its page name.

The commodity page shows inset text: "You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an health certificate."
claims.quote:
text: "You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. 
      You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an health certificate.",
claims.note: The source says "an health certificate". The earlier ITAHC wording is commented out at lines 42-45.

claims.statement: The commodity page's back link goes to /origin-of-the-import, or to the notification hub when opened from the hub, or to the template review when editing a template from review.
The commodity search field is labelled "Search for a commodity".
For live animals (and any type other than germinal products), the commodity search hint is "You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus)."
claims.quote: return 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).'

claims.statement: For germinal products in DR2.1, the commodity search hint is "You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985)."
claims.quote: return 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).'

claims.statement: The commodity search is a search box with a search button ("Search", visually hidden text), a results list labelled "Commodity search results" and a polite live region for status messages.
The commodity search box shows an inline error (prefixed "Error:" for screen readers) when the server sets a commoditySearch error, and the box is described by its hint and status region.
claims.quote: aria-describedby="commodity-search-hint commodity-search-status{% if data.errors and data.errors.commoditySearch %} commodity-search-error{% endif %}"

claims.statement: The commodity page shows the user's selections in a panel with a heading and a "Clear all" button that is hidden until something is selected.
claims.note: The heading element is empty in the view; its text is set client-side. "Clear all" is the button text.

claims.statement: The commodity page submits its selections in hidden fields: a commodity id, a commodity code, the selected species and the full list of selections.
claims.quote:
<input type="hidden" name="commodityId" class="app-commodity-search__commodity-id">
          <input type="hidden" name="commodityCode" class="app-commodity-search__commodity-code">
          <input type="hidden" name="selectedSpecies" class="app-commodity-search__species-value">
          <input type="hidden" name="commoditySelections" class="app-commodity-search__selections-value">

claims.statement: How the commodity and country searches behave in the browser (matching, result layout, picking species, the selection panel heading, removing a single selection) is not defined in the server code or views this source scopes in.
claims.note: app/assets/ is out of scope; the traces source covers client behaviour.

claims.statement: In DR2.1 the commodity search lists only germinal-product commodities when the notification type is germinal products, and only live-animal commodities when it is live animals.

In DR2.1, for live animals the commodity search offers the generated live-animal list plus four extra commodities (Gamebirds: day-old chicks, Gamebirds: adult birds, Poultry: day-old chicks, Poultry: adult birds), all sorted by name.
claims.note: hasJourneyUpdates is true whenever the DR2.1 flag is set.

claims.statement: For plants for planting, potatoes, wood products, or no type, the DR2.1 commodity search has nothing to offer, so a user on those types cannot select a commodity and cannot pass the commodity page's validation.
The commodity page gives the search a list of common English animal names (/public/data/common-names-live.json) only for live animals in DR2.1; for germinal products or any other type it gives none.

Commodity search results are sorted alphabetically by commodity name, and each commodity's species are sorted by "common name (Latin name)", or by "commodity name (Latin name)" when a species has no common name.
claims.note: Sorting ignores case and accents (sensitivity: 'base').

claims.statement: Each commodity search entry offers the commodity's id, name, code and species, and each species its id, Latin name and (where it has one) common name.
claims.quote:
id: commodity.id,
      name: commodity.name,
      code: commodity.code,

claims.statement: Each commodity search entry also carries the commodity's search terms and its full tariff codes where it has them, and each species its search terms, so search can match other names and codes beyond the name, Latin name and main code.
The commodity page opens with the notification's existing selections already chosen, filtered to those that match the current notification type.

The commodity page's pre-chosen selections can include whole commodities as well as species: saved selections of either kind are restored, and with none saved it falls back to the saved species, then to the saved main commodity.

The commodity page has a "Help with commodity codes" details component explaining: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers." and "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods."
claims.note: Paragraph quotes: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers." and "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods."

claims.statement: The commodity code help says "You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab).", linking to https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff in a new tab.
claims.quote:
You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool
(opens in a new tab).

claims.statement: The commodity page uses the default journey buttons: "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to overview" button and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification hub, because it sets no options of its own.
claims.note: When creating a template, the shared actions read "Save and return to template" and "Cancel and return to template" instead.

claims.statement: If nothing is selected, the commodity page shows the error "Select a commodity", inline and in the summary, linking to the commodity search box.

The commodity page passes validation with either selected species or a list of selections, so a whole commodity chosen with no species passes; that commodity is then kept in the saved list of selections, while the saved species list stays empty.
claims.note: mechanism: works on selectedSpecies and commoditySelections in the session. Origin-of-the-import and later pages that read only species (hasCommoditySelection) would treat such a notification as having no commodity.

claims.statement: A notification counts as having a commodity selection only when at least one species is selected.
Pages after the commodity page can be opened without a commodity selection: the guard against a missing commodity never redirects.
Submitted species and selections that do not belong to the notification's type are dropped before saving (for example, a germinal-product species on a live-animals notification).
A commodity belongs to germinal products if it is flagged as a germinal product; every other commodity belongs to live animals; for any other notification type, all commodities match.
Species ids that match no known species are dropped when the selection is saved.
Selected species may be submitted as a list, a JSON array, a single JSON string or a comma-separated string.
claims.note: mechanism: parses the selectedSpecies form value. An object of values is also accepted.

claims.statement: The saved selection records each selected species with its commodity id, commodity code and species id.
claims.quote:
type: 'species',
        commodityId: match.commodity.id,
        commodityCode: match.commodity.code,
        speciesId

claims.statement: The notification's main commodity (id, code and name) is the commodity of the first selected species; with no species it is cleared.
When every selected species is under commodity code 01061900 (cat, dog, ferret or other live mammals), any unweaned animals answer is cleared.

Saving the commodity page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves any valid species selection, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or review page.

After a valid commodity selection, the user goes on to /reason-for-import, or back to the hub, review or template review as the entry point dictates; when creating a template, the user goes to the notification hub.
Removing a species from the selection also removes its number of animals, number of packages, germinal packages, net weight and package type.
Removing a commodity removes all of its selected species, along with each species' number of animals, number of packages, germinal packages, net weight and package type.
claims.note: The routes that call these removals are in other parts.

claims.statement: Removing the last selected species or commodity clears the notification's main commodity id, code and name.
claims.quote:
if (speciesIds.length === 0) {
    sessionData.commodityId = null
    sessionData.commodityCode = null
    sessionData.commodityName = null

claims.statement: A selected commodity is summarised as "code (name)", for example "0102 (Cattle)".
A selected species is titled "code (common name - Latin name)", using the commodity name when the species has no common name, for example "0102 (Domestic cattle - Bos taurus)".

A species' label in a list of selected species is its Latin name, or its common name when it has no Latin name; in DR2.1, when the page asks for the updated label, it leads with the common name as "common name (Latin name)", unless the common name only repeats the commodity name or the Latin name.
claims.quote:
// Pass sessionData to get the label the updated versions show, which leads
// with the common name: "African sacred ibis (Threskiornis aethiopicus)".
claims.note: Which pages pass sessionData is decided in other parts' handlers.

claims.statement: Species and commodities are looked up by id across the generated live-animal list, the germinal-product list and the four extra gamebird and poultry commodities together; the code says the extra ones are included so their species can be looked up, while only the DR2.1 search offers them.

A commodity looked up by code returns the first commodity with that code, although several commodities share codes (most germinal products share 05119985; both gamebird commodities share 01063980; both poultry commodities show 0105; cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals share 01061900's identifiers).
claims.note: mechanism: code lookup over allCommodities. The live list's own codes are in the generated file this part does not read, so the 01061900 sharing is inferred from the curated identifiers.

claims.statement: The live-animal commodity list is a generated file plus hand-written fields: each commodity is given its curated fields by id (identifiers, purposes, unweaned options, packaging, permanent address flag), or empty identifiers when it has none, and the list is sorted by name.
According to its README, the generated live list holds live animals, including live crustaceans and molluscs: 48 commodities and 856 species.
claims.quote: | `commodities-live.json` | Live animals, including live crustaceans and molluscs: 48 commodities, 856 species |

claims.statement: According to its README, the generated germinal list holds germinal products (semen, embryos, ova and hatching eggs): 18 commodities and 29 species.
claims.quote: | `commodities-germinal.json` | Germinal products (semen, embryos, ova and hatching eggs): 18 commodities, 29 species |

claims.statement: The germinal list holds no hatching eggs entry, although the README says it covers hatching eggs: its 18 commodities are semen and embryos/ova only.
claims.quote: Germinal products (semen, embryos, ova and hatching eggs)
claims.note: Recorded as an ambiguity inside the source, not reconciled.

claims.statement: The commodity list is built outside the prototype from Defra commodity master data (October 2023 snapshot), the Defra notification test environment (read November 2026), the UK Trade Tariff headings 0101 to 0106 and 0511 (read 16 November 2026), the Defra EU import route data, the GOV.UK BTOM risk categories (updated 1 April 2025), the EU TRACES species list (9 November 2018) and the prototype's earlier list.
claims.quote:
| Defra commodity master data | October 2023 snapshot |
| Defra notification test environment | Read November 2026 |
| UK Trade Tariff, headings 0101 to 0106 and 0511 | Read 16 November 2026 |

claims.statement: Finfish are left out of the commodity list (headings 0301 to 0305 and code 0511.91.90); live crustaceans (0306.31 to 0306.39) and molluscs (0307) are in, but the dried, salted and smoked crustacean codes (0306.91 to 0306.99) are not.
claims.quote:
Finfish are left out: headings 0301 to 0305 and code 0511.91.90.
Live crustaceans (0306.31 to 0306.39) and molluscs (0307) are in. The dried, salted and smoked crustacean codes (0306.91 to 0306.99) are not.

claims.statement: Compared with the earlier list, the live list grew from 21 to 48 commodities (28 new, ornamental fish removed) and from 144 to 856 species (715 new, 3 fish removed); the germinal list grew from 15 to 18 commodities and from 22 to 29 species.
claims.quote:
| Live commodities | 48 (was 21). 28 new, ornamental fish removed. |
| Live species | 856 (was 144). 715 new, 3 fish removed. |
| Germinal commodities | 18 (was 15). 3 new. |
| Germinal species | 29 (was 22). 7 new. |

claims.statement: 85 Latin names sit under more than one live commodity.
claims.quote: | Latin names under more than one live commodity | 85 |

claims.statement: Every earlier commodity and species keeps its id, label and common name, in the same order, because journeys, templates and tests refer to them; an existing id must never change.
claims.quote:
Every earlier commodity and species keeps its id, label and common name, in the same order.
Journeys, templates and tests refer to them.

claims.statement: Many commodity and species names are generated: 28 commodity names are friendly names written for the list (the tariff wording kept separately), 3 follow the germinal naming pattern, and 616 species common names were written for the list and checked.
claims.quote: | Commodity `nameSource` | `generated` | A friendly name written for this list. The tariff wording is kept in `tariffDescription`. | 28 |

claims.statement: Species common names also come from Defra data: 23 for the same species under the same code, 39 for the same species under another code, and 9 matched by genus.

ITIS data is public domain, as a work of the US government, so no credit line is needed.

- A new `id` is lower case letters, numbers and hyphens, and is unique across both files.
- A commodity always has at least one species.

claims.statement: Cattle and pig commodities carry an unweaned animals question with Yes and No options; sheep, goat, horse and the companion mammals do not.
Cattle, pig, sheep and goat offer the purposes Approved bodies, Breeding and/or production, and Slaughter.
Horse offers the purposes Breeding, Racing/Competition, Registered equidae, Rejected or Returned consignment, Transit, and Other.
Cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals offer the purposes Approved bodies, Breeding and/or production, Circus/exhibition, Pets, and Other, and use the 01061900 identifiers.
Cat, dog and ferret commodities are marked as needing a permanent address; Other live mammals, which shares their identifiers and purposes, is not.

The amphibian, arachnid and reptile germinal commodities are named after the existing germinal pattern, and their tariff wording is only "Other / Other / Other / Other".

Germinal commodities can be found by search terms for the animal and the product, such as "cat, cats, feline" with "embryo, embryos, ova, ovum" for Cat, Embryos/Ova, or "semen, sperm, straws" for semen.

Where a germinal commodity has 10-digit tariff codes, semen is 0511998510, embryos/ova are 0511998520, the amphibian, arachnid and reptile embryos are 0511998590, and Cattle, Semen is 0511100000; the cat, dog and rabbit/rodent entries carry no tariff codes.
No germinal product is offered for any poultry, fish, bee or other-live-mammal species, and there is no Rabbit/Rodent Embryos/Ova entry: the 18 entries list none.
